opus-5.5.text:
I think the starting point is that when someone opts in, they're not just a data source, they're a participant. They're contributing something that has real value, and the system should treat them that way.

So first, transparency. People should know exactly what they're contributing, how it's going to be used, and who gets access to it. Not a forty-page terms of service nobody reads, but something clear: here's what you're sharing, here's what it trains or powers, here's how long it's kept.

Second, control. Opting in shouldn't be a one-way door. You should be able to see what you've contributed, change your mind, and ideally revoke access going forward. Part of what we think about in the user-owned AI space is that you hold the keys, not the platform. Your data lives with you, and you grant permission rather than handing it over.

Third, and this gets overlooked a lot, value should flow back. Right now the model is that users generate enormous value, and it gets captured almost entirely by a few large companies. If your data improves a model, there should be some way for you to benefit, whether that's direct compensation, ownership in the network, or better services built for you. Blockchain-based systems are actually useful here because you can track contributions and route rewards in a verifiable way, without trusting one intermediary to be fair.

And finally, privacy by design. Opting in to contribute shouldn't mean giving up privacy. With things like confidential computing and secure enclaves, you can let a model learn from your data without anyone, including the operator, seeing the raw data.

So in short: respect, transparency, control, and a fair share of the value. If we get that right, I think far more people would willingly contribute, and we'd end up with better AI for everyone.

r001.rationale: The response says users’ contributions should return value to them, such as compensation, network ownership, or better services.

fable-5.1.text:
I think the core principle is that users should be treated as owners and stakeholders, not as raw material. Right now the default model is that you sign a terms of service nobody reads, your data goes into a black box, and some company captures all the value from it. If someone is opting in to contribute, that relationship should be fundamentally different.

First, it should be genuinely consensual and transparent. People should know what they're contributing, what it's going to be used for, and what model or product comes out of it. Not buried in legal language, but actually understandable.

Second, they should have ongoing control. Opting in shouldn't be a one-way door. If you contributed data to train something and you decide later you don't want to participate, there should be a mechanism to withdraw, and ideally that's enforceable technically rather than just as a promise.

Third, and this is the part I care most about, they should share in the upside. If a model gets built on contributions from millions of people and it generates value, those people should get a piece of that. That's where I think the crypto and open-source side becomes relevant, because you can actually track attribution and route rewards back to contributors in a way that's verifiable and doesn't depend on trusting a single company to do the right thing.

So the short version is: treat contributors like participants in a shared project. Give them visibility, give them control, and give them a stake. If we do that, I think a lot more people would be willing to contribute, and we'd end up with AI that's actually aligned with the people whose data made it possible.

r001.rationale: The response says contributors should share in the upside and receive a piece of the value, including rewards routed back to them.

astra-6.text: I think users should have control over their data, and if they choose to contribute it, they should share in the value that it creates. You’re helping build something—you’re providing a resource that makes the system more useful. So you should understand what your data will be used for, be able to decide whether you want to participate, and get rewarded for that contribution. It should be a transparent relationship where the user is a participant, rather than just a source of data.

r001.rationale: The response says users who contribute should “share in the value” and “get rewarded” for their contribution.

sol-6.1.text: I think users should have ownership and control over their data. If they opt in to contribute it, they should understand what it’s being used for and share in the value it creates. You’re contributing something that makes the system better, so you should be treated as a participant in that system, with a say in how your contribution is used.

r001.rationale: It says users who contribute should “share in the value” their data creates, clearly communicating that they should receive something in return.
